candidates.commercialTrigger: CLDT 10-K YE2025 franchise schedule: Residence Inn Long Island Holtsville Marriott franchise expires 2026 — earliest property-level franchise expiration in the disclosed schedule.
candidates.decisionEvidence: Hotel-specific franchise expiration year from primary owner 10-K schedule. Expiration alone ≠ open RFP; Emerging early BCT. Operator is IHM (CEO-related) — MCT not the thesis.

commercialThesis.whatIsHappening: Marriott franchise for Holtsville Residence Inn reaches expiration in 2026 per CLDT franchise schedule.
commercialThesis.whyOpportunity: Owner must renew, renegotiate, rebrand, or sell around that franchise milestone.
commercialThesis.ownerObjective: Upscale extended-stay / select-service REIT; CapEx including brand PIP contemplated in 2026 budget (~$26.5M portfolio).
commercialThesis.existingRelationship: Residence Inn brand; day-to-day managed by IHM (100% owned by CEO Jeffrey Fisher) — related-party operator lock for MCT.
commercialThesis.whyAlternativePartner: Franchise economics and brand fit for Long Island extended-stay can be discussed before another multi-year lock-in.
commercialThesis.whatCouldPreventChange: Routine Marriott renewal; related-party IHM continues regardless of brand; no public dissatisfaction.
commercialThesis.whoControls: Jeffrey H. Fisher (Chairman/President/CEO); Jeremy B. Wegner (SVP/CFO).
commercialThesis.discussionAngle: Franchise fee/PIP path for Holtsville; soft-brand or competing extended-stay franchise options — not a management pitch against IHM without cause.

candidates.hotelName: Braemar Hotels & Resorts — Self-Managed Operator Reset Portfolio (parent)
candidates.commercialTrigger: Nov 10, 2026: Braemar terminated Ashford advisory agreement and Remington master hotel management / Premier project management agreements; transitioned to self-managed REIT. Sofitel Chicago → Stonebridge Companies; Cameo Beverly Hills → Avion Hospitality (committed replacements). Remaining brand-managed luxury hotels may see future operator/franchise reviews under independent board.
candidates.decisionEvidence: Primary owner press + 8-K path. Sofitel/Cameo operator selections are COMMITTED (closed). Portfolio thesis = relationship with newly independent Stockton-led team for future luxury operator/brand decisions — not all 13 hotels open.

commercialThesis.whatIsHappening: Braemar exited Ashford/Remington platform and is now self-managed with new third-party managers on two franchise hotels.
commercialThesis.whyOpportunity: Governance and operator reset often precedes selective brand/operator reviews across a luxury portfolio.
commercialThesis.ownerObjective: Luxury urban/resort RevPAR growth; self-management cost/control narrative.
commercialThesis.existingRelationship: Mix of brand managers (Marriott/Hilton/Four Seasons/Hyatt) plus new Stonebridge/Avion on franchise assets.
commercialThesis.whyAlternativePartner: Owner demonstrated willingness to change management structure (brand-managed→franchise Sofitel May 2025; Remington exit Nov 2026).
commercialThesis.whatCouldPreventChange: Long brand management agreements on many assets; Sofitel/Cameo already re-awarded.
commercialThesis.timing: Build relationship now during governance transition; monitor property-level contract schedules.
commercialThesis.whoControls: Richard J. Stockton (President & CEO; continuing director).
commercialThesis.discussionAngle: Luxury operator platforms and soft-brand options for assets where contracts allow; respect committed Stonebridge/Avion assignments.
commercialThesis.evidenceBasis: Braemar Nov 2026 self-managed press release; prior Sofitel franchise conversion Apr/May 2025

candidates.hotelName: Crowne Plaza Atlanta Perimeter at Ravinia
candidates.commercialTrigger: SVC IHG management agreement for sole Crowne Plaza (Atlanta Perimeter / Ravinia, 495 keys) expires January 31, 2027. Q2 2026 earnings: SVC intends to market the hotel for sale; expiration provides buyer optionality with or without brand. Not an SVC-retained conversion RFP.
candidates.decisionEvidence: Verified HMA expiration + owner sale process. Commercial opportunity is primarily for (a) prospective buyers evaluating brand/operator and (b) brands/operators who can engage the sale process — NOT a claim that SVC will reflag while retaining. Expiration alone ≠ Verified conversion.

commercialThesis.whatIsHappening: SVC is bringing its only IHG-managed hotel to market as the IHG agreement approaches Jan 31, 2027 expiry.
commercialThesis.whyOpportunity: Buyer can purchase with brand optionality; competing brands/operators can engage sale advisors and buyer pool.
commercialThesis.ownerObjective: Unlock shareholder value via sale vs hold/reinvest (Bilotto commentary).
commercialThesis.existingRelationship: IHG Crowne Plaza management; returns limited to available cash flow after expenses.
commercialThesis.whyAlternativePartner: Post-sale affiliation is unresolved; agreement expiry gives flexibility.
commercialThesis.whatCouldPreventChange: Buyer may keep Crowne Plaza; sale timing/pricing may slip; SVC may re-hold.
commercialThesis.timing: Engage now through early 2027 sale/expiry window.
commercialThesis.whoControls: SVC via RMR (Chris Bilotto commentary on earnings); Brian E. Donley CFO.
commercialThesis.discussionAngle: Brand/operator packages for Atlanta full-service buyers; do not pitch SVC as retaining and converting.
commercialThesis.evidenceBasis: SVC 10-Q IHG expiry Jan 31, 2027; Q2 2026 earnings sale marketing
